caveats: Only two original synthetic train parents (701,702) and two dev parents (801,802), all derived from one historical template. Four primary training pairs contain only two nonzero effects; six resource training pairs contain four nonzero effects. Fleet descendants and multiple opportunities do not create additional independent parents.

Targets are realized 1800-second paired differences J_ref-J_patch under the fixed continuation. All retained natural successors have singleton support. This is paired score-difference regression / finite-window Monte Carlo ranking, not demonstrated optimal multi-step Q learning or bootstrap FQI.

C01 and C11 use exactly the same actually executed pairs and train/dev snapshots; C11 adds a causally gated frozen forecast to 29 current features, giving 43 features. The old prepared 88-dimensional feature benchmark is a different model family.

Forecast parameters are reused from historical source day 2026-09-01, made available at synthetic source time 43200. Target dates are declared experiment coordinates; static schedules are retrospectively identified and assumed supplied at startup. This establishes the declared experimental clock contract, not independent real airport days or original real-world publication timestamps.

All primary-domain chosen models have development known harm 16 and mean paired regret 620.21225 bag-seconds, exceeding both the reference-rule and always-patch controls on regret. Lower training loss alone does not establish useful anticipatory dispatch.

Development harm counts cover only mutually completed jobs. Unknown/incomplete counts remain large and are sums of pair-level populations, not unique bags across parents. Zero selected known harm, where present, does not certify nonharm.
Failure means selected attempted transfer lacks a positive delivered ACK; zero failure does not imply every requested end-to-end policy objective succeeded.

Development evaluation chooses between the two saved actions independently at each paired opportunity. It is not a native rollout of the learned full-horizon policy; there is no native policy benefit claim in this audit.

Selection is lexicographic: failures, known harm, mean regret, parameter count, then model ID. Seeds are retained separately; there is no best-seed selection. Candidate architectures use the same dev pairs, so reported dev metrics are selection metrics, not unbiased test performance.
No test datasets or test outcomes were opened by this audit. Source and training/selection manifests remain frozen.

development_conclusions.selection_tradeoff: Known harm precedes regret. For mixed C01 seed17, the small MLP has harm11/regret1146.5433 versus linear harm17/regret413.4748, so MLP is correctly selected despite higher regret. Similar tradeoffs explain several other mixed-domain MLP selections.
development_conclusions.interpretation: Protocol and provenance checks pass; these development results do not establish an anticipatory scheduling benefit from adding the forecast or training a ranker. Native prospective evaluation is separate and remains unread by this audit.

metric_definitions.mean_paired_regret_bag_seconds: Mean over saved dev pairs of max(0, actual J_ref-J_patch) minus actual advantage if patch selected; baseline choice contributes gain0. Unit is bag-seconds, not a percentage or seconds per bag.
metric_definitions.selected_known_harmed_jobs: Sum of per-pair harmed counts only when patch selected. Missing harmed key is accepted as0 only after complete count container and full population are validated. Counts repeat bags across paired scenarios.
metric_definitions.selected_failure_count: Sum over selected actual attempts whose positive_delivered_ack is false.
metric_definitions.pair_unknown_incomplete_jobs: Sum of unknown_incomplete across all saved pairs independent of choice; do not interpret as a unique-bag count.
metric_definitions.selection_candidates: Exactly linear and small MLP within each domain/variant/seed. Reference and always-patch are diagnostics, not model selection candidates.
